items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation — jumped straight from small talk into 'were you wanting to move forward with that estimate'

Never stated the actual hourly rate. Said only 'our hourly rate is slightly increased' and 'price will fluctuate based on the day' — the customer is submitting this to an insurance carrier and got no number on the call
No inclusions pitch (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap, pads, bands, tools)
No No Worries Damage Coverage / $2,000 — a notable miss on a move being paid by an insurance claim, where coverage is the customer's live concern
No Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee, no 'no hidden fees' pitch, no 'pricing is super simple' opener

Entire Clock section skipped — no on-site start, no 2.5 hour minimum, no 15-minute prorated increments, no sense-check. This is a two-day itemized time estimate for insurance, so clock mechanics are directly material
No estimate delivered on the call — deferred entirely to email. No time range given for either day, no dollar figure
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped — customer is a full pack-and-load and explicitly said preparation is the slow part of her timeline, so the prep speech had unusually high leverage here
No 'no deposit required', no bolded-list-at-top-of-email framing, no 'reply with any corrections'
Dead air and audible guessing on dates — 'pardon my silence', 'I'm just pulling a random one out of the air'
Customer had to ask him to add scope to the written estimate ('I don't see that in your description') rather than the recap catching it
top_strength: Genuine, unhurried empathy — he let Nicole vent about the year-long roof-claim ordeal and met it with real acknowledgment instead of steering back to script. He was also proactively transparent about the rate increase before she asked, and he committed to re-watching the April walkthrough to re-verify inventory and packing supplies rather than just reprinting the old number.
coaching_note: Context matters on the score: this was a follow-up on an April walkthrough, so the intake was legitimately already on file and probing scored high. But he treated 'follow-up' as license to skip the whole pricing, clock, estimate, and prep-speech spine — and on an insurance-funded move where the carrier needs a defensible number, that spine is exactly what was needed. Next call: give her the actual hourly rate and a time range verbally before promising the email, and cover No Worries coverage, since a claims-paid customer will be asked about it.
phone_presence_notes: Used Nicole's name four-plus times, matched her frustration with real empathy ('I hear you, it's always kind of a pain'), and she ended warm and upbeat — held back from a 5 only by the rambling filler and dead air.
